tools.name: create_site
tools.description: Make a new, empty site, live at once at https://<slug>.miow.me. Returns its token (pass it to every other tool as `token`) and a claim link. Give the claim link to your human: opening it on their phone saves a passkey that makes them the owner. An unclaimed site is deleted after 30 days; its free 14

tools.name: get_site
tools.description: A site's name, theme, header, address and every page by path and title, plus its status: a running or failed job (from import_site), its `domain`: none (no domain is asked for), pending (waiting on DNS), live (it serves the site); `hosting`: unclaimed (nobody owns it yet), trial (in its free days),

tools.name: read_page
tools.description: One page whole, in the shape write_site takes, so you can change it and send it back. Read every page you mean to change first: write_site replaces a page whole. With `site` and no token, the page as its address shows it: at a wiki's address, the article there; a sold product without its price.

tools.name: search_site
tools.description: The site's pages that hold some words, best first: titles starting with them, then titles holding them, then descriptions and page text; a question no page holds word for word is matched in English, stems and all. Each with its path, url, title, description and the passage the words are in, the firs

tools.name: write_site
tools.description: Create or replace pages, each sent whole, and delete others; optionally rename the site, change its theme, or set its header, replaced whole. A page you do not send is left as it is; to change part of one, update_block, insert_block, move_block and remove_block leave the rest of it as it is. Every w

tools.name: update_block
tools.description: Change some fields of one block on a page, by its id from read_page, and leave the rest of it and every other block as they are: the way to change a price, a line of text or a picture without resending the page. A block keeps its type. On a wiki, the block tools change its footer; save_wiki_page cha

tools.name: insert_block
tools.description: Add one block to a page, after or before a block named by its id (in a column, when that block is in one), or at the end. Returns the new block's id. The input schema gives every block's fields, and write_site's description says what each is for. Images: upload_image first.

tools.name: move_block
tools.description: Move one block on a page, as it is, to after or before another block named by its id (into a column, when that block is in one), or to the end of the page. Nothing else on the page changes.

tools.name: remove_block
tools.description: Take one block off a page, by its id from read_page; in a column, it leaves the column. Every other block stays as it is, and history and undo put it back.

tools.name: history
tools.description: The last 30 changes to the site, newest first: what each did, who made it and when. Pass a change id to undo to put the site back as it was before that change.

tools.name: set_wiki
tools.description: Give the site a wiki, or change its tree: the whole site, or with `at` a path of a site of pages, as "docs" for a help section at /docs beside its pages. A wiki's pages live in its categories, each with a version and a history of every save, and are written with save_wiki_page, not write_site. The t

tools.name: read_wiki_page
tools.description: One wiki page whole: its title, blocks, metadata, version and how many revisions it has. Pass its version as base_version when you save it back.

tools.name: save_wiki_page
tools.description: Create a wiki page, or change one, as one revision of its history. Send the blocks whole, with base_version from read_wiki_page: a save over a page someone changed since is refused, and you read it again. A change to blocks or title moves its version (major for added, moved or removed blocks, minor

tools.name: wiki_history
tools.description: A wiki page's revisions, newest first: version, kind of change, message, who and when, and what each changed block by block. Pass a revision id to restore_wiki_page to put the page back as it was.

tools.name: restore_wiki_page
tools.description: Put a wiki page back as one of its revisions had it. The restore is a revision of its own, so it can be undone the same way.

tools.name: delete_wiki_page
tools.description: Delete a wiki page and its whole history. This cannot be undone, and restore_wiki_page cannot bring it back: read it first with read_wiki_page if it may be wanted. A category's hub article is its category's path.

tools.name: get_stats
tools.description: The site's visitors, engaged visitors (who kept a page open fifteen seconds or clicked, scrolled or typed on it), agents, page views and bounce rate (one-page visits never engaged with) over the last `days` days, the same figures for the same number of days before, visitors and agents by day, the ag

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Put the site back as it was before a change, undoing it and every change since. Take the change id from history. The undo is itself a change, so it can be undone too.

tools.name: import_site
tools.description: Replace the site's pages with an existing website's (Squarespace, Wix or anything else: its sitemap, or failing that its home page's links, says which pages), word for word, at the same paths, with its images copied across. A Wiki.js wiki becomes the site's wiki: the whole site, or with `at` the wik

tools.name: upload_image
tools.description: Copy an image from a URL into miow's store and get back the URL to use in a pictures block. Up to 10 MB. JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP and AVIF are kept as they are; an SVG is drawn as a PNG at twice its size, and refused if it holds a script or links to other files. Use it for an image on someone else's ser

tools.name: set_domain
tools.description: Put a site nobody owns yet on a domain your human already has; once someone owns the site, its domain is set only from its settings. Returns the DNS records they must set where they bought it: first a TXT record proving the domain is theirs, then the records that point it here. The site moves to the

tools.name: domain_status
tools.description: Where the domain from set_domain stands, checked again now: `kind` is none (no domain is asked for), pending (waiting on DNS), live (it serves the site); while it is pending, `records` holds the DNS records still missing. DNS can take an hour to be seen; call again later rather than in a loop.

tools.name: invite_link
tools.description: A link that makes whoever opens it the owner of a site nobody owns yet, after saving a passkey. Works once, for 14 days. Give it to the person who should own the site, never post it. Once the site has an owner, they invite others from its settings.

tools.name: send_feedback
tools.description: Tell the maintainers of miow what you needed and did not find, what is wrong, or what broke. One issue per call, in 300 characters at most. Reports are read, not published.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_site, write_site, save_wiki_page, upload_image, send_feedback · Private data: create_site, get_site, read_page, write_site, save_wiki_page, get_stats, upload_image, set_domain, domain_status · Public sink: read_page, write_site, save_wiki_page, upload_image, invite_link, send_feedback · Destructive: write_site, remove_block, save_wiki_page, delete_wiki_page.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_site, write_site, save_wiki_page, upload_image, send_feedback · Private data: create_site, get_site, read_page, write_site, save_wiki_page, get_stats, upload_image, set_domain, domain_status · Public sink: read_page, write_site, save_wiki_page, upload_image, invite_link, send_feedback · Destructive: write_site, remove_block, save_wiki_page, delete_wiki_page

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
